summary: Osterquill capability overview distinguishing exploratory rat range finding and non-GLP in vitro screening from regulated GLP investigations. It explains control validity, individual-animal traceability, welfare oversight and independent QA gates.

slides.title: Safety portfolio and investigation pathways
slides.subtitle:
Osterquill Toxicology Inc | Portland | 05/19/2025
Dr N. Takamori, Head of Toxicology

slides.title: Start with the decision the package must support
bullets: Early chemistry triage, dose selection and regulated safety conclusions require different investigation designs.
Define the compliance scope before accepting test articles.
Control validity, animal welfare oversight and traceability apply throughout; a non-GLP screen does not become GLP through report formatting.

slides.title: Exploratory versus regulated work
bullets: Non-GLP in vitro screens rank a test article cohort.
Exploratory rat range finding informs dose selection and tolerability.
Limit conclusions to the tested conditions and available exposure.
bullets_right: GLP investigations follow an approved plan and controlled amendments.
Independent QA examines conduct and reporting.
The signed report identifies compliance scope and departures.

slides.title: hERG (IKr) safety pharmacology
bullets: Whole-cell patch clamp measures concentration-dependent current inhibition.
Report potency in µM with evaluable concentration limits and cell-level qualifications.
Reference-control acceptance precedes test article ranking.
Interpret in relation to unbound exposure; screening alone cannot establish a clinical safety margin.

slides.title: CYP safety interaction panel
bullets: Evaluate inhibition across CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6 and CYP3A4.
A fixed-concentration result identifies follow-up needs.
CYP3A4 follow-up IC50 resolves concentration dependence for selected test articles.
Record probe, reference control and historical comparison; do not infer mechanism from the initial panel.

slides.title: HepG2 viability screen
bullets: ATP-content response provides a cellular viability endpoint.
Exposure duration, solvent and concentration coverage accompany each result.
Check assay interference before interpreting reduced signal as toxicity.
Use the screen to qualify later decisions, rather than extrapolating directly to whole-animal tolerability.

slides.title: Genetic toxicology
bullets: Bacterial mutation assay with and without S9 addresses activation-dependent responses.
Mammalian-cell micronucleus assessment retains proliferation and cytotoxicity context.
Vehicle and positive controls must support each treatment condition.
Kenji Morita provides scientific interpretation; uncertain exposure-related findings require a defined repeat.

slides.title: Exploratory rat range finding
bullets: Rat DRF and recovery supports selection of doses and observation schedules.
Express dose in mg/kg/day and retain dose-lot traceability.
Individual-animal identifiers remain visible in observations, weight changes and pathology links.
Exploratory findings guide design; they do not constitute a regulated GLP conclusion.

slides.title: Animal welfare before and during exposure
bullets: Define welfare observations, intervention criteria and escalation responsibilities before dosing.
Promptly communicate a concerning observation to the responsible Study Director and designated welfare personnel.
Document the observation time, intervention and subsequent condition on the animal card.
Welfare action must not await the next scheduled QA gate.

slides.title: Control validity: a scientific release condition
bullets: Define acceptance criteria before acquiring the test article measurements.
Retain rejected runs and explain repetition; present only accepted measurements as interpretable results.
Flag concentration limitations and interference alongside the result.
Do not suppress a qualification because a client needs a rapid decision.

boxes: Test article receipt > Dose-lot and identity reconciliation
Conduct > Control validity and welfare review

slides.title: Roles and independence
bullets: Dr N. Takamori: portfolio oversight and scientific escalation.
Rachel Okafor: Toxicology Study Director; investigation conduct and conclusions.
Lucia Moretti: independent GLP Quality Assurance and archive control.
Kirsty Greenwood: sample management; Nathan Wade: pathology coordination.
Scientific authors resolve findings; QA retains independent reporting of its observations.

slides.title: Report and archive handover
bullets: State the tested cohort, conditions, compliance scope and limitations early.
Link summary findings to observation sheets, animal cards and dose lots.
Retain original entries, amendments, control-validity evidence and report approval history.
Separate exploratory recommendations from signed regulated conclusions.

slides.title: Scope discussion with Osterquill
bullets: Provide the intended decision, test article identity, available exposure information and material constraints.
Agree assay endpoints and the requested compliance scope before scheduling.
For in vivo work, establish dose rationale, welfare provisions and recovery objectives.
Dr N. Takamori and the responsible Study Director will define the investigation and QA gates.
